items.title: Lanny Morgan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999
items.q: It was Bill Perkins first and then Joe Lopes, the first couple of years.

ctx.x: How much time would you have to get that ready?

Well I wasn’t on the original SuperSax. It was Bill Perkins first and then Joe Lopes, the first couple of years. They spent a year rehearsing in Perk’s garage before they even ventured outside. But see the band doesn’t work anymore, that’s the trouble. So Med’s got a band, a big band, with seven or eight brass and the sax is SuperSax in front, and then the L.A. voices too. Well that’s like a 19-piece band, and it’s hard to even book a trio in this town let alone a 19 piece band. So he’s put all his effort into…

several years. As a result SuperSax is not working, not doing anything. When we were working quite a bit, even three or four times a month, this stuff was easy. But I mean well it was not easy but everyone had it under their fingers, even the inner parts. But you know we’ll get a gig now and Med will call maybe a three-hour rehearsal and we’ll go over some of these things, but you can’t begin to get all those things. I mean it’s not only this, there’s a whole host of those things that are really very difficult.…
